subject: history_social
passage: In Bangladesh, mobile banking services let people send, receive and save money using a basic phone. Economist Tahmina Akter surveyed villages in Rangpur Division in 2018 and again in 2022. She reports that younger adults were still the most likely to use mobile banking in 2022, but that the gap between age groups narrowed because use grew fastest among adults aged 50 and older.

data.title: Village Residents Using Mobile Banking in Rangpur Division, by Age Group

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support Akter's explanation of why the gap narrowed?

choices.A: The share of residents aged 18–29 who used mobile banking rose by more percentage points between 2018 and 2022 than did the share of any other age group.
choices.B: In 2022, 74 percent of residents aged 18–29 used mobile banking, the highest share of any age group that year.
choices.C: In both 2018 and 2022, residents aged 30–49 used mobile banking at a higher rate than residents aged 50 and older.
choices.D: The share of residents aged 50 and older who used mobile banking rose from 12 percent to 41 percent, a larger increase than in either younger age group.

explanation.why: Akter explains the narrowing gap by saying that use grew fastest among adults aged 50 and older, so the support must compare the increases of the age groups. The oldest group rose from 12 to 41 percent (29 points), more than the 18–29 group (16 points) or the 30–49 group (19 points).
explanation.A: Incorrect. The 18–29 group rose by only 16 points, the smallest increase of the three, so this misreads the graph.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true and matches Akter's point that younger adults were still the most likely users, but it does not show why the gap narrowed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is true, but it describes a difference that existed in both years; it does not show which group's use grew fastest.
explanation.D: Correct. The oldest group rose by 29 percentage points, compared with 16 for ages 18–29 and 19 for ages 30–49, which shows that use grew fastest among older adults.
